newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa jails two for life for Christmas massacre.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa jails two for life for Christmas massacre.

text.p: A South African judge on Thursday jailed two men for life for a "savage and barbaric" massacre of 18 people on Christmas Day, 1995.
The men were among a 1,000-strong group that swept through Shobashobane on the Indian Ocean coast, killing 18 supporters of President Nelson Mandela's African National Congress.

"The deed brought enormous shame to our entire country...you showed the outside world a residue of the savage and barbaric behaviour that we hoped we had left behind," Judge Hilary Squires told the court.

He gave the heaviest sentences to two local leaders of the mainly Zulu Inkatha Freedom Party, as an example to warring factions in the Zulu heartland, where about 15,000 people have been killed in political violence since the mid-1980s.

"You will be made an example of so that any other local leader or warlord who sets in motion or is party to this sort of violence will know what awaits them," Squires told Inkatha leaders Sipho Ngcobo, 43, and Zithulele Zuma, 30.
He ordered that they be jailed for life.
Ten other accused were sentenced to terms ranging from eight to 15 years for their part in the violence.

Children, women and men were shot, stabbed and clubbed to death after being chased into an ambush by two columns of men encircling them in a pincer movement, a Zulu war manoeuvre perfected over a century ago.
Squires rejected defence arguments that ANC supporters had provoked the attack.
"There was no difference of race or religion...this is called ethnic cleansing in other parts of the world and that is what has shamed us all," he said.
A large crowd of ANC supporters cheered when the sentence was handed down and outside the court people danced and sang before dispersing.
